Single-cell RNA-seq: young vs aged human skin

Example report made with Claude and the BRC plugin

Author

Bioinformatics Resource Center, Rockefeller University

Published

November 10, 2026

NoteAbout this report

Everything here was produced in a single Claude session with the BRC plugin, which gives Claude access to single-cell datasets hosted by the BRC (here 76 datasets) and tools to query and plot them. The prompts used are shown in each section.

Data: public dataset GSE130973, human skin from 2 young and 3 older donors. Solé-Boldo et al. (2020) Single-cell transcriptomes of the human skin reveal age-related loss of fibroblast priming. Commun Biol 3:188. doi:10.1038/s42003-020-0922-4

1. What’s in the dataset?

“Load the young vs aged skin dataset and give me a QC summary per donor.”

Donor Age Cells Median genes per cell Median UMIs per cell Median mito % 95th percentile mito %
S1 Young 2784 1194 3155 2.46 4.45
S2 Young 2670 1082 2697 2.07 4.09
S3 Old 3324 1492 4077 1.41 2.84
S4 Old 2144 1133 2935 2.60 4.38
S5 Old 4535 754 1651 1.50 3.09

What Claude found: 15,457 cells from 5 donors. Mitochondrial reads are low for every donor (median 1.4-2.6%), so there is no sign of many dying cells. Donor S5 (old) has the most cells but the fewest genes and UMIs per cell, so its cells were sequenced less deeply. Keep that in mind when comparing ages: with only 2 young and 3 old donors, one donor can drive a difference.

2. Clusters and age

“Show me the UMAP coloured by cluster, and again by age.”

3. What cell types are the clusters?

“Make a dot plot of skin cell-type markers across the clusters and suggest a cell type for each.”

Cluster Proposed cell type Marker evidence Cells
0 Myeloid LYZ 1930
1 Fibroblasts COL1A1, APOD 1886
2 Fibroblasts APOD, COL1A1 1793
3 Fibroblasts COL1A1, APOD, PDGFRA 1675
4 Endothelial (vascular) CLDN5, VWF 1467
5 Keratinocytes KRT10 (differentiating) 1399
6 T cells CD3D, PTPRC 1281
7 Keratinocytes KRT14 (basal) 1069
8 Pericytes / smooth muscle ACTA2, RGS5 722
9 Fibroblasts COL1A1 594
10 Pericytes / smooth muscle ACTA2, RGS5 498
11 Unclear (low quality?) Few genes per cell; 271 of 310 cells from one donor 310
12 Endothelial (lymphatic) CLDN5, LYVE1 294
13 Myeloid LYZ 227
14 Melanocytes PMEL 123
15 Keratinocytes KRT14, KRT10 118
16 Myeloid LYZ 71

What Claude found: fibroblasts are the largest group (clusters 1, 2, 3 and 9), as expected for a dermis-rich sample, alongside myeloid cells, endothelial cells, keratinocytes, T cells, pericytes and a small melanocyte cluster. Cluster 11 is suspicious: its cells express few genes, and almost all of them come from one donor (S2), which looks like a technical artefact rather than a cell type.

Tip

These labels are Claude’s suggestions from a handful of markers, a starting point, not a final annotation. Check them against the paper and a reference atlas, and ask the BRC if you need a formal annotation.

4. Does cell-type composition change with age?

“Compare the proportion of each cell type between young and old donors, per donor.”

% of each donor’s cells
celltype S1 S2 S3 S4 S5
Endothelial (lymphatic) 1.4 1.0 3.0 2.2 1.8
Endothelial (vascular) 5.2 11.0 15.3 9.2 7.1
Fibroblasts 32.4 33.3 35.6 27.6 52.5
Keratinocytes 7.5 3.8 20.6 45.9 13.4
Melanocytes 0.6 0.7 1.4 0.8 0.6
Myeloid 17.8 6.9 14.5 9.0 19.2
Pericytes / smooth muscle 13.4 16.3 6.6 3.5 2.6
T cells 21.6 16.9 2.4 1.0 2.8
Unclear (low quality?) 0.0 10.1 0.4 0.7 0.2

What Claude found: T cells make up 17-22% of the cells from both young donors but only 1-3% of cells from each old donor, a consistent difference in all five donors. Other shifts are driven mainly by single donors: for example, much of keratinocyte cluster 5 comes from old donor S4. Composition depends on how each biopsy was taken and dissociated, so these are leads to follow up, not conclusions.

What the BRC plugin did

Step What you ask What happens behind the scenes
Find data “What single-cell datasets are available?” Lists the scRNA-seq datasets the BRC hosts
Load “Load the young vs aged skin dataset” Activates the dataset on the BRC server
QC and counts “QC per donor”, “cells per cluster per donor” Read-only queries of the cell metadata
Plots “UMAP by age”, “dot plot of markers” The server draws the plots from the full expression data
Markers “What genes differ between clusters?” Runs a marker test on the server
Report “Put it all in one report” Writes this page

The expression data never leave the BRC server. Claude only sees the summaries and plots it asks for.

WarningBefore you use results like these
  • Single-cell results depend on choices made upstream: filtering, clustering resolution and integration. The clusters here are the ones supplied with the dataset.
  • Cell-level statistics treat thousands of cells as independent, which overstates confidence. Compare donors, not cells, and talk to the BRC about the right test.
